# Rule revision and actual generation with open forms

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

Along a run of a frame, where completion is decided, each unfinished step lowers the current rule's remaining-step certificate, each handoff to a revised rule at the stage reached does not raise it, the initial certificate is at most B, and each completion corresponds to new living content, the run realizes, within B + 1 steps, living content absent before. Under the continuation condition the same realized content falls under the relevance read from significance; its form is not fixed in advance or across runs. Witnesses: each rule kept finishes within two steps and each unfinished step lowers its own remaining count, yet revised at every step the run never completes, each revision resetting the remaining count from 1 to 2; a revision can change the formed outcome and still meet the handoff bound, and the realized form need not be fixed.

Canonical source: [Handoff.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Handoff.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- Actual indexed histories, steps, natural-number certificates, decidable completion events and an initial bound are supplied; unfinished local descent and non-increasing handoff at the same reached stage are separate hypotheses.
- Completion corresponds to actual newly formed generative content in the same history, with different content allowed across histories. The conditional law takes the continuation condition (Unrestricted) as a hypothesis; significance is not derived from progress.
- Transport from admitted scope to actuality requires actual coverage and execution/support correspondence. Permission, real losses and still-valid specific undertakings require judgment under existing practical principles.

Stages, organizational rules and revisions differentiate within shared activity, without a primitive external controller or private value owners. Certificates support a specified finite realization bound; if event n denotes transition n to n+1, events 0..B comprise at most B+1 transitions. Terminal states named formed do not themselves certify actual goodness or fulfillment.
